title: Y1DA--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base  573-27-702-DB EHRM Generator Upgrades Design-Build -  Gainesville VAMC
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > PCAC HEALTH INFORMATION (36C776)
description:
SYNOPSIS:

INTRODUCTION: 
This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of performing a Design-Build (DB) project. Services to include Architect and Engineering (DB A/E) design services, site preparation and DB Construction (DB C) services for the construction of Emergency Power Generator Upgrade for Electronic Health Record Modernization at the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in Gainesville, Florida.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
The Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (Gainesville VAMC) has a requirement to design and construct an Emergency Power Generator Upgrade to support Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) at the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center. 

This Design-Build Team (DBT) shall provide all design and construction services, investigations, labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, permits, temporary emergency power, demolition, lawful disposal, site improvements, testing, commissioning, training, and documentation necessary to deliver a complete turnkey Emergency Power Generator Upgrade for EHRM at MRVAMC. The DBT shall evaluate existing conditions and deliver a code-compliant operational emergency power system while protecting the existing Emergency Power Switchboard and maintaining required hospital emergency power capability throughout construction, subject only to specifically approved planned switching windows.

The facility's existing 1,275 kW emergency generator (Generator #5) reportedly operates at approximately 85% load; the Contractor shall independently verify actual demand and operating conditions. Planned EHRM infrastructure is estimated to add 150-200 kW of critical load, including IDF/telecommunications closets and associated cooling; the Hybrid OR project is estimated to add approximately 100 kW of emergency loads. These figures are planning estimates, not verified design loads. The replacement generator shall be rated at not less than 2,000 kW and selected to provide at least 10% unused rated kW capacity after accounting for verified coincident operating demand, planned loads, and site derating.

The DBT shall provide a complete enclosed generator and all required fuel, exhaust, switchgear interface, ATS, distribution, monitoring, platform, site, and temporary emergency power work. Existing generator site boundaries are constrained; significant expansion to the north or south is not anticipated to be feasible. The DBT shall confirm the usable footprint and design a solution accordingly.

PROCUREMENT INFORMATION:
The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 36.101-2, Use of two-phase design-build selection procedures. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process.

This project is planned for advertising in mid-January 2026. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $5,000.000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 238210 (size standard $19.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all design and construction related services. 


CAPABILITY STATEMENT:
Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: 
Section 1: Provide company name, DUNS number and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email.

Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 238210. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). 

Section 3: Provide a statement of interest in the project.

Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above.

Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: 

Provide a maximum of three (3) projects completed within the last ten years (10) years in which the Offeror s design-build team has worked together on previous design-build contracts similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. Projects must demonstrate a respondent s design-build experience as a prime construction contractor directly responsible to the owner and managing multiple subcontractors. NOTE: If a prime contractor does not have Design-Build experience, they are permitted to provide up to three (3) relevant non-Design-Build projects that are completed in clinical, hospital or other medical related use space similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. 

The designer for the team may also provide up to three (3) relevant projects that fall under the requested criteria for the project. 

A maximum total of six (6) projects may be submitted between the D-B and design teams. *All submission requirements for these projects remain the same and are listed above.
